rv.q: The masterful strokes of playwright Dominque Morisseau, the visionary leadership of director Raymond O. Caldwell, and a brilliant tour de force cast make Confederates a crowning achievement at the Fountain Theatre.

What comes across instead is a reductive melodrama, with mugging from the performers in place of a skilled delineation of their characters’ truths — as essential in farce as it is in kitchen sink drama.
